maria: Quick q — for continuous batcher: prefer global heap-ordered prefetch queue or stable per-lane queues for hot prefixes? thinking about latency tail vs packing. cc @jon @kevin
jon: Short answer: tradeoffs. Heap -> best packing and token efficiency but higher jitter for hot tenants. Stable lanes -> predictable latency, worse packing for skewed workloads.
kevin: Also memory churn with global heap during KV warmup. In our proto tests p50 stable, p99 went up ~15-20% with heap under bursty tenants.
alexa: Do you have the sim logs? can we run a controlled sim with synthetic tenant skew and short vs long seqs?
maria: Tossing a tiny snapshot from my run (staging): p99 jumps when heap merges bursts. snippet: ```config
prefetch.heap_enabled=true
prefetch.heap_max=4096
lane_count=8
```
jon: If heap is global, eviction/compaction causes pauses. One thought: hybrid -> per-lane mini-heaps + global compaction sweep. Keeps lane isolation while benefiting from packing.
kevin: Hybrid looks promising but increases admission/scheduler complexity. We need a clean enqueue API (e.g., `enqueue(req, deadline_hint, tenant_id)`) that returns a small `lease` so batcher internals can decide lane vs heap.
alexa: We have `enqueue` proto already but it assumes a fixed lane mapping. We can extend it with `deadline_hint` and `prefetch_hint` without breaking callers. Observability is key: per-lane headroom, heap_occupancy, kv_warmup_count so ops can tune.
infra-bot: ALERT: metric batcher.heap_sweep_duration spiked to 300ms in staging at 12:08 UTC (recent deploy: r-2026.03.20).
sam: :eyes: saw that spike. It synced with a tenant-replay job that flooded short requests. Heap compaction took the hit.
maria: Proposal: default to stable lanes for Hosted (lowest tail risk). Offer `heap-hybrid` as an opt-in flag for Dedicated and Private, toggled by config + autoscaler tuning. Document rollout and opt-in criteria.
jon: Another mitigation: route interactive short requests probabilistically to stable lanes and batch/long sequences to heap/hybrid. That reduces jitter for interactive paths.
kevin: Agree. Also need to ensure prefix/KV caching semantics unchanged — mixing lanes must preserve KV-cache locality.
alexa: I'll draft a short RFC with diagrams: API changes, hybrid architecture, observability additions, and a perf plan. Timeline idea: prototype this sprint, run perf sweep next sprint, gate for Dedicated.
maria: Action items: @alexa write RFC, @jon prototype lane-miniheap, @kevin add perf harness and tests, @sam validate staging alerts and add dashboards. I'll update rollout checklist and opt-in docs.
sam: Ack. I'll schedule a 20m sync tomorrow 10:00 for quick alignment.
jon: One last note — keep a fallback: if heap compaction > X ms, degrade to stable lanes automatically. Avoid noisy neighbor p99 regressions. :thumbsup:
